title: Longitudinal changes in mis-splicing in a cohort of female twins are widespread and highlight mechanisms of ageing - Nature Communications
byline: Wang; Dongmeng; Raza; Yasrab N; Roberts; Amy L; Bowyer; Ruth C E; Ramisch; Anna; Tomlinson; Max; Shore; Christopher J; Yan; Xinyu; Dermitzakis; Emmanouil T; Ste
html:
Abstract

Ageing is characterised by widespread cellular and molecular dysregulation including broad changes to gene expression. To study the impact of ageing on alternative splicing we profiled whole-blood RNA-seq data from 318 female twins (median age 61) at three time points over 6-8 years. We observe longitudinal changes across multiple classes of alternative splicing. Notably, intron retention, a marker of mis-splicing, shows a striking increase over time (P = 5.2 × 10−5). Twin modelling demonstrates that intron retention within an individual is heritable, with heritability increasing from 0.44 to 0.55 over time. Intron retention levels inversely associate with expression of RNA-binding proteins including SRSF4, ELAVL1, and AGO1, and show time-varying positive associations with diabetes status and markers of kidney disease, suggesting a link to chronic disease. Together, these findings suggest that mis-splicing is a heritable feature of human ageing which increases in prevalence over time and is associated with age-related disease.
